**Curated fallback may still offer EOL Claude Opus 4 profile**

Keeping `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-20250514-v1:0` in `CURATED` offers an uninvocable model as a pick, the very defect this PR fixes, and makes the comment's guarantee false. Check that snapshot and `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-1-20250805-v1:0` against the Bedrock lifecycle page, then drop any that are EOL.



<details>
<summary>Prompt for LLM</summary>

````text
File libs/llm/providers/bedrock/listing.ts, lines 7-9:

Curated fallback may still offer EOL Claude Opus 4 profile

The rewritten comment claims all EOL profiles are excluded, but the very same hunk keeps `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-20250514-v1:0` (line 14) — Claude Opus 4 shares the identical `20250514` snapshot generation with the removed `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-20250514-v1:0`, and AWS/Anthropic retire paired Sonnet/Opus snapshots under one lifecycle schedule. If Opus 4 carries the same EOL date as its removed sibling, this fallback still offers an uninvocable, EOL model as a pick — the exact defect this PR set out to fix — and the comment's guarantee is false. Verify `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-20250514-v1:0` (and, while there, `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-1-20250805-v1:0`) against the same Bedrock model lifecycle page and drop it from `CURATED` if it is EOL.
````

</details>


<sub>Talk to Kody by mentioning @kody</sub>


<sub>Was this suggestion helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to help Kody learn from this interaction.</sub>
